title: Meta's Muse gains a 33% share of AI browser traffic in 9 days, DataDome finds
key_facts: DataDome's Q3 2026 report counts nearly 25 billion AI agent requests, up from 17.7 billion in Q2 (up 41.5%).
Agentic browser requests rose from about 12.5 million in August to 58.2 million in September (4.7x).
Muse took 33% of agentic browser requests in September, from nine days of detection; 29.1 million Muse requests between 22 Sep and 3 Oct.
99.3% of sampled Muse requests came from cloud and CDN infrastructure; 0.6% from consumer ISPs.
8.9% of Muse requests hit sensitive flows such as forms, logins, payments.
Meta's crawlers were 49.7% of AI agent traffic in Q3; ClaudeBot grew 159%.
Figures are DataDome's own and unaudited; network size not stated; Profound's earlier claim that Muse uses residential connections conflicts with DataDome's sample.
quote_evidence: The numbers in the report are DataDome's own, drawn from traffic crossing its bot-management network, and they have not been independently audited.
"Muse is not a standalone browser," according to the report.
why_it_matters_hint: Shows how fast cloud-run AI agents are becoming a web traffic class that existing bot checks may miss.
